## Historical audit — S0329

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/test/bw_0056/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines in that file. The supplied observations contain whole lines, not split observations.

**Goal versus evidence:** The requested goal was a photograph-matched, editable indoor reconstruction, including camera, framing, geometry, and materials (line 1, H model request). The student interpreted the scene as a cleanroom packaging line with two workers; that interpretation and its image bounds are student estimates, not independently observed image facts (line 3, H response).

| Event | Evidence and limits |
|---|---|
| Initial build | H generated named room, machine, conveyor, HMI, and two person assets with child meshes. The code specifies a raised arm, HMI support, translucent guards, colored surfaces, roughness, and area lights; it does not independently verify physical connections, pose, textures, or appearance (lines 3–4). |
| First validation and revision | Build and render completed; step 1 was selected (lines 6–10). The student reported a small foreground worker, indistinguishable background worker, low HMI, excessive floor, and pale closed-looking machine. It then changed camera, people, belt, HMI, and machine geometry (lines 11, 13–14). These are student visual assessments, not independent image verification. |
| Second validation and revision | Step 2 built and rendered successfully (lines 16–20). Its upward-aim trial moved projected points downward and was restored; this trial did **not** validate the earlier wholesale camera change (lines 13, 19). H then reported the foreground head still low and left, the background worker absent, and washed-out machinery; it changed people, camera, room, belt, HMI, lighting, and depth of field (lines 23–24). The extended hand and fingertips are coded toward the screen, but contact and a plausible arm are unverified. |
| Final execution | Step 3 built and rendered successfully and was selected (lines 26–30). On the revised geometry, the camera comparison projected the hairnet top at (0.307, 0.142) versus the student’s reference estimate (0.32, 0.01); the ceiling panel was (0.217, 0.289) versus (0.25, 0.16) (line 29). Projections are not visible-contour or material checks. No subsequent review or DONE is recorded. |

**Input and exploration:** The user supplied reference images, numerical projection instructions, and render-comparison prompts; the runner returned the first two renders and logs in subsequent H requests (lines 1, 11, 21). No separate teacher diagnosis or teacher-directed update is visible, so teacher receipt or adoption cannot be claimed. H autonomously produced two revisions and projection trials within that prompted workflow; its sessions record no independent tool calls (lines 2, 12, 22).

**Outcome and uncertainty:** There is formal execution success for all three builds, but final reconstruction correctness is **unknown**, not established by successful rendering or selection. The images themselves are unavailable in this audit; final object visibility, hand-to-screen contact, pose, material/texture fidelity, lighting, camera framing, and render artifacts remain unresolved. The student’s earlier diagnoses are hypotheses, and the final render was not visibly reviewed.

**Transferable lesson:** Comparing several foreground and background projections can expose directional framing discrepancies, but cannot substitute for image or connection checks. **Task-specific lesson:** The reported worker placement and dark machinery motivated local revisions here; whether those revisions improved the final image remains unverified.
